metadata.title: Sandisk shares slide 8% despite earnings beat as investors weigh valuation

content.text:
Sandisk Corporation (NASDAQ:SNDK) shares fell around 8% in morning trading on Friday despite reporting first-quarter results that topped Wall Street expectations, as investors weighed strong datacenter demand against the stock's sharp rally and concerns about the broader memory market.
The shares have gained approximately 460% year to date, raising expectations for the flash memory maker and leaving little room for disappointment. The pullback also coincided with a broader sell-off in memory stocks, with Western Digital down 8%, Seagate falling 7% and Micron losing 6%.
Sandisk reported revenue of $11.03 billion for the quarter, up 378% from a year earlier and ahead of analysts' consensus estimate of $10.64 billion.
Adjusted earnings per share came in at $49.51, compared with expectations of $46.22. Adjusted gross margin reached 85.1%, up 55.2 percentage points year over year and ahead of the 84.1% forecast. Adjusted operating income was $8.87 billion, exceeding the $8.44 billion estimate.
Datacenter revenue climbed to $4.80 billion, reflecting a 61% sequential increase as demand for memory used in AI infrastructure continued to strengthen.
Edge revenue rose 7% from the previous quarter to $5.83 billion, while consumer revenue declined 29% to $397 million, highlighting uneven conditions across the company's markets.
For the second quarter, Sandisk forecast revenue of $12.2 billion to $12.6 billion, above the $12.18 billion analyst consensus.
It expects adjusted earnings per share of $55 to $57, compared with estimates of $53.19, and adjusted gross margin of 84.5% to 85.5%.
The company also announced an eight-for-one forward stock split, effective November 19, 2026.
Sandisk repurchased approximately 3.2 million shares for $5 billion during the first quarter. Wedbush said the company has $10.5 billion remaining under its share repurchase authorization.
The brokerage maintained its Outperform rating and raised its fiscal 2027 and 2028 earnings per share estimates to $236.41 and $304.20, respectively, from $228.52 and $268.44. It also described Sandisk's pricing assumptions as conservative.
Jefferies pointed to continued strength in datacenter demand, forecasting that the segment will account for more than 55% of the NAND market in 2027, with bit demand expected to grow by roughly 40%.
However, the brokerage noted slower trends in edge and consumer markets, underscoring the importance of datacenter demand to Sandisk's growth outlook.
Friday's share price decline suggests investors are looking beyond the latest earnings beat to assess how much further growth is already reflected in the stock's valuation.
